title: Personal Sender Account Terms: Entry Requirements and Limit Review Terms of Each Level
content:
Each verification level of the Personal Sender Account has entry terms — how old the account must be and how many personal transfers it must have completed before it may move up to that level, and whether moving up to it needs a compliance limit review approval rather than an upgrade applied by a support agent — together with the terms that govern compliance limit reviews.

## Entry terms

| Level | Account age before moving up to this level (calendar days since the account opened, at least) | Completed personal transfers before moving up (at least) | Compliance limit review approval needed to enter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paloma Starter | 0 | 0 | no |
| Paloma Verified | 0 | 0 | no |
| Paloma Verified Plus | 30 | 2 | no |
| Paloma Enhanced | 90 | 5 | yes |
| Paloma Premier | 180 | 12 | yes |
| Paloma Private Client | 365 | 24 | yes |

## Limit review terms

| Level | Compliance review time when this level is the level requested (business days) | Cooldown after a declined limit review (calendar days) | Limit reviews that may be requested in a rolling 180 calendar days (most) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paloma Starter | 0 | 30 | 2 |
| Paloma Verified | 0 | 30 | 2 |
| Paloma Verified Plus | 0 | 30 | 2 |
| Paloma Enhanced | 3 | 60 | 2 |
| Paloma Premier | 5 | 90 | 3 |
| Paloma Private Client | 7 | 90 | 3 |

A compliance review time of 0 means the level is entered with no review at all.

## Points of reading

- **Two ways up.** The three lower levels are reached without any compliance review; Paloma Enhanced, Paloma Premier and Paloma Private Client are entered only with a compliance limit review approval.
- **The review time belongs to the requested level.** The review time column is read on the row of the level asked for, not the level the account already holds.
- **Account age and completed transfers are minimums.** An account opened 89 calendar days ago does not yet meet the 90-day age for Paloma Enhanced; at 90 days it does. The figures in this example are taken from the table; the account is hypothetical.
